clue.text: Bill doesn't have time to finish course 9

definitions.note: the answer to 9 across, a phrase meaning something fiery, used as the definition

parts.note: a tab is a bill run up at a bar or restaurant

indicators.note: doesn't have says a letter is taken away from the racecourse's name
to finish says the letter dropped sits at the end of that name

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse

explanation.surface: Someone runs out of time to finish a course, and the bill arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference '9', i.e. HOT STUFF. 'doesn't have ... to finish' removes the final T from ASCOT (an English racecourse) to leave ASCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a fiery chilli sauce, so it is literally spicy, burning stuff on the tongue.

clue.text: One dressing a sort of kebab includes minimal amount of rosemary

indicators.note: includes says one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a doner is a kind of kebab

indicators.note: a minimal amount of the herb is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone dresses a kebab with a pinch of rosemary.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the first letter of rosemary, goes inside DONER; A comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who decorates or embellishes, dressing something up, is an embellisher.

clue.text: Fool, say, topping spear

parts.note: an ass is a fool
say means for example, abbreviated eg
topping is old slang for excellent, i.e. A1, written AI

explanation.surface: A fool spears something to put on top, say.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written with I for the figure 1; 'topping' is dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped hardwood spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Fierce cat that can make a cur go crazy

indicators.note: crazy signals that the letters of the preceding words go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A fierce cat can send a dog mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges A CUR GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar, or puma, is a large wild American feline and a powerful predator.

clue.text: Paper flower's suffering from heat, naturally

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
a flower is something that flows, a river or stream; a burn is a Scottish stream

explanation.surface: A newspaper's flower piece wilts in the summer heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but 'something that flows', a crossword stock word for a river; BURN is the Scottish word for a stream. The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin reddened by too much exposure to the sun's rays is the natural result of heat from that star.

clue.text: Like either part of eternity ring?

definitions.text: Like either part of eternity ring?

parts.words: Like either part of eternity ring?
parts.note: eternity has no end, and neither has a ring, so the word describes both halves of the jeweller's phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Never stopping or everlasting describes both eternity and the circle of a ring.

clue.text: Page 23's written down after objection

indicators.note: in a down answer, written down after means placed below, so this piece follows

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no buts
the answer to 23 down is a hundred, and a ton is a hundred, so the plural is tons

explanation.surface: A page's notes are written below an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is HUNDRED, so '23's' means hundreds, TONS. Buttons is the page in the Cinderella pantomime, a British Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is slang for a pageboy, from the rows of buttons on his uniform jacket.

clue.text: Rule lifted after French man's restoration

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the Frenchman

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name

indicators.note: lifted in a down answer means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A rule is lifted to help restore a Frenchman's property.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'lifted' means read upwards, so the rule is reversed; 'after' places it below the Frenchman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoring something to a fresh state is to make it new again.

clue.text: Goods handled by fence whose performance is remarkable?

explanation.surface: A receiver of stolen property turns out to be a star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is a criminal who buys and sells stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen loot that a receiver (fence) deals in is slang 'hot' merchandise; a person or act that is impressive or exciting is also called by this phrase.

clue.text: Street seen by many in West End

definitions.text: Street seen by many in West End

parts.words: Street seen by many in West End
parts.note: the musical about a Broadway chorus girl, named after a Manhattan street, has played to huge audiences in London's theatre district

explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district, so a 'street' seen there is a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York thoroughfare names a stage musical seen by many theatregoers in London.

clue.text: Epicure's opening a can anticipating good this?

definitions.text: Epicure's opening a can anticipating good this?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from the gourmet

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A gourmet opens a can, looking forward to a good meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: E (Epicure's opening), A, TIN (can) placed before ('anticipating') G (good). An epicure, opening a can and expecting something good, looks forward to this activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Consuming food is exactly what a gourmet opening a tin and hoping for a treat is about to do.

clue.text: Meaning, oddly, to drop one new puzzle

indicators.note: oddly signals the remaining letters are arranged in a strange new order
to drop tells you to take a letter out of the word before rearranging

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, and only one of the two in the word goes

explanation.surface: Someone finds an oddly worded new puzzle loses its meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like 'odd letters' but is the anagram signal. Dropping one N from MEANING leaves MEAING, which 'oddly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle or mystery that baffles is a puzzle, just as the famous wartime cipher machine was.

clue.text: I put in a word to change channel

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A listener puts in a word asking someone to switch the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges the letters of I, A WORD and TO. Radio Two is a BBC radio station.
explanation.definitionFit: BBC Radio 2 is a British radio station, and a station is a broadcasting channel.

clue.text: Powerful man trains, turning into a fighter

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

indicators.note: turning means the abbreviation for the railway is read backwards

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old UK national railway

explanation.surface: A powerful man trains hard and becomes a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses BR (British Rail) to RB, which goes 'into' MIG, the Russian fighter plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime boss or dominant figure is nicknamed Mr Big, the person at the top.

clue.text: Exclude from drinking establishment, using some pressure

explanation.definitionFit: To ban someone is to keep them out; a pub serving drinks; and a unit of air pressure used in weather forecasts.

clue.text: Boy seen misbehaving left female alone

indicators.note: misbehaving suggests the letters of boy and seen are behaving out of order

explanation.surface: A naughty boy is spotted leaving a woman on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' is the anagram signal for 'Boy seen'; 'left' and 'female' are standard single-letter abbreviations added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without company means being solitary, with nobody else present.

clue.text: Heading north, live for a long time

indicators.note: in a down answer heading north means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: are means live, exist, as in we are

explanation.surface: Someone heading north means to live there for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading north' reverses ARE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or epoch is a long period of history.

clue.text: New Age occasion

parts.note: the day on which someone reaches a new age, one year older, read instead of the spiritual movement

explanation.definitionFit: On the anniversary of your arrival in the world you start a fresh year of life.

clue.text: Twice I perused translation of Greek dramatist

indicators.note: translation of means the letters are turned into a different form, rearranged
twice tells you to write the following letter two times

explanation.surface: A student reads a Greek play twice while translating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' doubles I, and 'translation of' rearranges II with PERUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the three great tragedians of ancient Athens, writer of Medea.

clue.text: Man from Italy having to resettle in Burma

indicators.note: to resettle means the letters move house into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian man has to resettle in Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resettle' rearranges IN BURMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a region of central Italy, so a native is an Italian.

clue.text: One disregards caterer on giving boxes back

indicators.note: back says the enclosed letters are read in reverse
boxes means the words enclose the letters within them

explanation.surface: Someone takes no notice when the caterer brings the boxes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' picks RERONGI from 'caterer on giving'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pays no attention and takes no notice is one who disregards.

clue.text: Wrap small fruit, then large

parts.note: a haw is the red berry of the hawthorn
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Instructions for wrapping fruit, first small then large.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap is a loose garment draped over the shoulders, like a stole.

clue.text: Division of county seen three times in Clacton?

definitions.text: Division of county seen three times in Clacton?

parts.words: Division of county seen three times in Clacton?
parts.note: an old subdivision of an English shire, such as the one the Essex seaside resort lies in, also written as the Roman letter C

explanation.walkthrough: Clacton is a resort in Essex, in the old Tendring district; C is the Roman numeral for a hundred and appears in the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shires were historically divided into districts each said to hold a hundred households.

clue.text: Punishment? Why?

explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a severe telling-off is to give them a phrase meaning a scolding; asked as a question, it means for what reason.

clue.text: Traps underwater, primarily a problem for divers

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of the word underwater

parts.note: the bends is decompression sickness, a danger to divers who surface too fast

explanation.surface: Underwater traps are mainly a problem for divers.
explanation.walkthrough: Plumbers call the curved pipe under a sink that holds water a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped section of drainpipe holds water to stop smells, which plumbers call a trap.

clue.text: From the start, a short life's work's contained in it

indicators.note: contained says one piece sits within another

parts.note: a biography is a work about a life, shortened to bio
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brief biography holds within it the whole story from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips the 'life's work' (a biography) to its familiar short form, and 'contained' puts 'in it' inside that after its first letter; the 's of work's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means from the beginning, used for starting over afresh.

clue.text: Nut by one, said to be a dwarf tree

indicators.note: said to be signals that the pieces must be spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: nut is slang for head, which is bonce in British slang; one is I

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a tree back until it is said to be a dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for the head (also 'nut'); BONCE with I (one) beside it is heard as the tree's name. The scan's 'Cut' is a misread of 'Nut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots, and the term names such a tree.

clue.text: Hunter's game stuck on pole

parts.note: nim is a game of taking matchsticks or counters
a rod is a pole, as in a fishing rod

explanation.surface: A hunter's quarry is impaled on a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Hunter's stands for 'is'. Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Nimrod is described as a mighty hunter, so his name means a skilled huntsman.

clue.text: Falling flakes fop's not unknown to get on collar

indicators.note: not says the following letter is left out of the dandy

parts.note: a fop is a dandy, a man vain about clothes
Y is a mathematical unknown, like X
a ruff is a stiff frilled collar

explanation.surface: Flakes fall on a dandy's collar and he is well aware of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' means the fop loses his algebraic unknown, the letter mathematicians use alongside X; the collar then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurf from the scalp drops off in little white scales that settle on the shoulders.

clue.text: Is binding books on flatfish? There's work to be done here

definitions.text: There's work to be done here

indicators.note: binding says the outer letters wrap around the other pieces

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
a ray is a flat-bodied fish

explanation.surface: A bookbinder covers volumes with fish skin, and there is plenty of work waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: IS 'binding' NT (New Testament books) and RAY. The definition describes trays on an office desk holding papers awaiting attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Office trays hold incoming papers yet to be dealt with, the pending jobs.

clue.text: Woman, one finding blue mineral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
blue means sad or down
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A woman feels low on discovering a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadore is a given name, here one borne by a female.
